title: DWR-1: The Dual-Write Receipt — Simultaneous Dual-Rail Storage of a 32-Byte Digest on Bitcoin and XRPL Mainnets Under One Joint Commitment (Ceremony Specification and Runlog)
description:
SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Errors are disclosed, not erased. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All payloads are hashes; no customer-identifiable data appears in this record (POL-DISC-001).

DWR-1: the first Dual-Write Receipt — the same 32-byte SHA-256 digest stored simultaneously on the Bitcoin and XRPL mainnets under one joint prior commitment. Prior ceremonies in this corpus bound artifacts to Bitcoin via OP_RETURN and carried digests across XRPL custody round trips. DWR-1 upgrades the doctrine to dual-write STORAGE: no custody transfer anywhere. The Bitcoin leg is an OP_RETURN postage-only write (684 sats, entire input consumed as fee, no change output). The XRPL leg is the corpus's first NON-PAYMENT write: an AccountSet carrying the digest in a memo — the ledger as a data store, not a payment rail (10 drops, no value moved). Because no protocol provides cross-chain atomicity, the deterministic substitute is joint prior commitment: both transaction ids were frozen in a hashed pre-registration BEFORE either broadcast; broadcast interval 0.3 seconds. A mempool policy gate caught a non-canonical DER signature in the first commitment and rejected it pre-broadcast — nothing touched any chain; the defect and amendment are disclosed in the record. Keyless readers on both rails return the payload byte-exact (XRP validated ledger 107754612). The artifact is the specification itself (self-referential, per the Satoshi Embodiment precedent). Full runlog, preregistrations, and executable scripts included.
